clue.text: Capital articles gain points

blocks.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles
N and S, north and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Items of capital spending gain value on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a big letter, but it is a nation's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek seat of government is a national chief city, the usual crossword sense of capital.

clue.text: “His — s dark as Erebus" (Mer, of Venice)

blocks.note: surface: a line from The Merchant of Venice with a word missing
setter's reading: supply the missing word from Lorenzo's speech on music, 'And his ... dark as Erebus'

explanation.walkthrough: Lorenzo says the man with no music in himself has spirits dull as night and feelings dark as Erebus, the gloomy underworld; the blank takes the plural, so the entry is the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Shakespeare's line means feelings or inclinations, here the inner disposition of an unmusical man.

clue.text: Gather for this festival

blocks.note: first meaning: to reap and bring in a crop
second meaning: the word that goes before festival in the church thanksgiving for crops

explanation.surface: Assemble for the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The harvest festival is a thanksgiving service held in British churches in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap crops is to gather them in, and the same word names the autumn thanksgiving celebration.

clue.text: Garment to put on after dark

indicators.note: after says one piece comes later, so the words before it are written second

blocks.note: the dark hours are night
to put on clothes is to dress

explanation.surface: Clothing to wear for an evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests evening wear for a party, but the garment is worn to bed; read 'put on' as a verb placed after 'dark'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's loose gown for sleeping in is an item of clothing, so it is a garment.

clue.text: Is opposed to computers

blocks.note: first meaning: argues against or opposes in return
second meaning: people or devices that reckon numbers, taking computers in its literal sense

explanation.surface: Someone is against computers, a technophobe of the 1980s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computers' suggests machines, but here it means anything that computes or tallies, as a vote counter does.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means opposes or resists, while the noun names people who tally numbers, literal computers.

clue.text: Thor got so mad at this barbarian

indicators.note: something mad is crazy and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: The Norse thunder god was furious with a barbarian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were an eastern Germanic tribe that overran Italy, so a member is a barbarian to the Romans.

clue.text: Number one in France is not a proper example

definitions.note: names a common example of the answer, one that is not a proper one

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
un is the French for one

explanation.surface: France's leading figure is not a fitting model.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar a word is either proper, naming one particular thing, or common; the clue defines the part of speech by an example that is not proper.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming word in grammar is proper or common, so a common one is an instance of the part of speech that isn't proper.

clue.text: State train

blocks.note: first meaning: to put into words
second meaning: a fast railway service with few stops

explanation.surface: A nationalised railway service.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice or put into words is to state, and a fast non-stopping railway service bears the same name.

clue.text: Found paving block raised

blocks.note: a set or sett is a stone block for paving
raised means up

explanation.surface: A paving stone has been discovered lifted out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as discovered, but it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company or charity is to establish it, which is to set it up.

clue.text: Flower having raised scarlet ring

indicators.note: in a down entry something raised reads upward, so it runs backwards

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A bloom with a lifted bright red ring of petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick for a river, something that flows; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and the Oder is a major central European river.

clue.text: Searched for food for OAPs?

blocks.note: taken as written
OAPs, old age pensioners, are the aged

explanation.surface: Someone hunted out meals for pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is British shorthand for an old age pensioner, so the aged; the question mark flags the split of the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to hunt about for provisions, so the past tense matches searched for provisions.

clue.text: Proclaim the execution of a whore

indicators.note: an execution here is a beheading, so the word that follows loses its head

blocks.note: strumpet is an old word for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A town crier announces that a prostitute is to be put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: STRUMPET beheaded leaves TRUMPET.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly and publicly, as a herald with a horn would.

clue.text: Writer's city style

blocks.note: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England
ton is fashionable style, from the French

explanation.surface: An author's urban manner of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay. Ton, meaning the fashionable mode, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was the English author of the Father Brown detective stories, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Tom did squeak

blocks.note: first meaning: what ... Tom did, looking secretly at Lady Godiva
second meaning: a small high cry, as a chick or mouse makes

explanation.surface: Tom the cat, or Tom of a cartoon, let out a squeak.
explanation.walkthrough: Peeping Tom of Coventry looked at Lady Godiva as she rode naked; the cartoon cat in the surface is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeping Tom's act was a sly look, and the same short word also names a tiny chirp or squeak.

clue.text: Make specific, as some doctors do

blocks.note: first meaning: to adapt or narrow to a particular purpose
second meaning: to concentrate on one field of medicine

explanation.surface: Doctors narrow their focus to one branch of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to narrow something to a particular use and to train in one field, like a consultant.

clue.text: Confines not more than one at a time, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken phrase, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

blocks.clueFragment: not more than one at a time
blocks.note: doing things one after another, in sequence

explanation.surface: A rule limits people to entering singly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in turns' is said to sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to detain them, especially in wartime, so it means confines or imprisons.

clue.text: Poor puss finished hanged

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the letters are in a sorry disarray

blocks.note: taken as written
finished means ended

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a cat that came to an end on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging something from above leaves it dangling in the air, so suspended matches hanged.

clue.text: A colleague of old, but hostile

blocks.note: oppo is British slang for a mate or colleague, short for opposite number
sed is the Latin for but, the language of old

explanation.surface: A former coworker who has turned against you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of old' points to Latin, where SED means but. An oppo is a colleague in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed is against a thing, set in antagonism toward it, hence hostile.

clue.text: ' Finds site disturbed as the Pied Piper did

definitions.note: describes the past action; the answer is the present-tense verb

indicators.note: disturbed means moved out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a place has been upset, as by the Pied Piper's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pied Piper of Hamelin piped the rats out of the town, ridding it of vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of rats or other pests is to clear it of vermin, which is what the Piper did for Hamelin.

clue.text: Stone me! Sister's part goddess

indicators.note: only a part of the words before it is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across stone, me and sister

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a sister's role, perhaps in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' is a British exclamation of astonishment; the answer is inside stoNE ME SISter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek deity of retribution, punishing hubris, so she is a goddess.

clue.text: Birdman captures a Wellsian invader

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: Martin is a man's name and also a bird of the swallow family
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aviator seizes an alien attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdman' suggests an aviator, but it is a man's name that is also a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds the invaders come from Mars, the red planet.

clue.text: Favours for Highlanders up in anger

definitions.note: describes the answer when raised, in the idiom 'hackles up'

blocks.note: first meaning: feather plumes worn on the bonnets of Highland regiments
second meaning: neck feathers or hairs that rise when an animal or person is angry

explanation.surface: Scottish soldiers wear tokens and get worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour is a ribbon or badge worn as a token; Highland regiments wore feather plumes called by this name in their bonnets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names cockade plumes in Scottish military dress and also the raised neck hairs that signal rage.

clue.text: Flower guaranteed for holiday

blocks.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
guaranteed means sure

explanation.surface: Flowers are certain to be part of a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Flower' is not a river; it stands for a garland of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work, which is what a vacation or break provides.

clue.text: Poet's bolted, so they say

indicators.note: what people say is speech, so the sound of the word counts here

blocks.note: a bolted door is barred

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a poet has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' suggests fleeing, but here it means locked with a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially a minstrel of Celtic tradition; Shakespeare is the Bard.

clue.text: The guiding principle for scholars is . . .

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so scholars are BAs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher begins stating the main principle for students, trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots lead into 25 down, making the two clues read as one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or underlying principle on which a system or argument rests.

clue.text: Production groups have empty container

indicators.note: one thing having another means holding it inside

blocks.note: genera are groups in biological classification, the plural of genus
a tin is a can or container
empty means holding nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: A film company's units have a box with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' is used as a noun here, standing for nothing, the round letter that goes inside the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The generation of power or ideas is its making, so the word is a synonym for creation or output.

clue.text: . . . it's always right to support a lady

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece supports another by sitting beneath it

blocks.note: Eve, the first woman, is a lady
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Continuing 23: it is always correct to give a woman a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, for evermore, the same as always.

clue.text: The fourth man was one of Starkadder's lads

blocks.note: first meaning: after Adam, Cain and Abel, the next male in Genesis
second meaning: a son of the Starkadder family in Cold Comfort Farm

explanation.walkthrough: Stella Gibbons's comic novel Cold Comfort Farm has the Starkadders, whose handsome son is obsessed with the talkies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam's third son is the fourth male person, and the name is shared by a Starkadder son.

clue.text: Payment to reverse mine's closure

indicators.note: to reverse is to run backwards, so the word after it is read from its end

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine, with the 's kept as an S
a closure is an end

explanation.surface: Compensation offered for reversing a colliery shutdown, in the year of pit closures.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit closures were front-page British news in the mid-1980s miners' strike era.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, as paid to a clergyman, so it is a payment.

clue.text: Concoct high class recipe for gourmet

indicators.note: to concoct is to mix up ingredients, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook devises a posh dish for a food lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' for upper class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of refined taste in food and wine, a synonym for gourmet.

clue.text: Star's had vitamin as protection against erythema

blocks.note: the sun is our star
taken as written
vitamin E

explanation.surface: A celebrity took vitamins to guard against skin reddening.
explanation.walkthrough: Erythema is reddening of the skin, as in sunburn; the star is a celebrity in the surface but the sun in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning blocks the sun's rays, guarding the skin against burning and reddening.

clue.text: Not long ago soldiers had very little money

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: Lately the troops were hard up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adverbial but the answer is an adjective; read as 'of not long ago'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent means lately happened, so it describes things from a short while back.
